title: Key cultural institutions funding and community capacity fund
subtitle: Committee also heard delegations from Oktoberfest and the Arts Fund, and discussed tracking list items and delegation time limits.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended terms of reference for the 2024 Community Capacity Building Fund {{vote:m1}}. The fund, backed by $1M in the 2024 budget, supports grassroots groups led by and serving First Nation, Métis, Inuit, Black, African, Caribbean and racialized communities. If Council adopts it, the 2024 funding cycle could open as early as March.

The main debate was over Key Cultural Institutions funding. Staff proposed splitting the $347,153 budget across four organizations. The committee instead recommended a $840,603 total allocation {{vote:m3}}, after first amending the motion so THEMUSEUM keeps its previous $385,725 {{vote:m4}}.

The extra $493,450 would come from the Tax Stabilization Reserve in 2024 and be added to the preliminary 2025 base budget, so it would affect the property tax levy next year. Staff said the reserve is under significant strain. Staff are also to review the KCI program and funding model with area municipalities and report back in 2024. All of these are recommendations to Regional Council.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the Terms of Reference for the annual Community Capacity Building Fund {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended a 2024 Key Cultural Institutions allocation of $840,603: $100,000 to Kitchener Waterloo Art Gallery, $93,587 to Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery, $261,291 to Drayton Entertainment and $385,725 to THEMUSEUM {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: THEMUSEUM funding held at prior level
decisions.detail: The committee amended the motion so THEMUSEUM stays at its previous $385,725 and the resulting $93,450 shortfall comes from the Tax Stabilization Reserve {{vote:m4}}.

The committee recommended funding the $493,450 above the 2024 budget from the Tax Stabilization Reserve and adding an incremental $493,450 to the Preliminary 2025 Base Budget from the property tax levy.

decisions.item: KCI program and funding model review
decisions.detail: The committee recommended directing staff to review the KCI program and funding model with the area municipal working group and report to Regional Council in 2024, ahead of 2025 funding requests.

debate: Supporters of the original motion argued that adding three new institutions to a smaller envelope had unintended consequences. They wanted the funding split on one consistent formula, so that all four organizations were treated equitably and nobody was singled out.

Backers of the amendment said cutting THEMUSEUM about a sixth of the way into the year could be devastating. They noted the three newer institutions had no funding history, while THEMUSEUM would lose existing funding. They also said the established collaborative approach with area municipalities should continue.

Some councillors said the repeated reopening of budget decisions was a concern. They said arts organizations need consistent, predictable funding, and called for a broader review of external grants and where else the arts are funded. Another councillor suggested that an outside community body could allocate arts funding.

Staff said the Tax Stabilization Reserve is under the most strain they have seen. Its year-end balance was estimated at around $12 million, which limits flexibility if something unexpected arises in 2024 and affects the 2025 budget. One councillor asked for a plain summary of what each reserve is for.

A THEMUSEUM delegate called the proposed reduction a 'gut punch' with four months left in its fiscal year, though it had met the conditions of an earlier business review early. Another councillor raised Cambridge's share of funding and asked about delegation time limits, while one councillor preferred strict equal time.
